he.t: אמור, ואמרת, להזהיר גדולים על הקטנים (יבמות קיד. — ת"כ פרשתא א, א):

en.t: Speak to the kohanim.
Say, and you shall say — to warn the adults regarding the minors.
The sons of Aharon.
Perhaps those unfit [are also included in this prohibition]? The verse says:
The kohanim. The sons of Aharon —
even those who have a [physical] blemish are implied.
The sons of Aharon,
and not the daughters of Aharon.

he.t: בעוד שהמת בתוך עמיו, יצא מת מצוה (ת"כ שם ג):

en.t: Let him not defile himself among his people,
while the dead body is still “among his people,” excluding a mes mitzvoh.
Except for his kin.
“His kin” [refers] to none other than his wife.

he.t: לרבות את הארוסה (שם יב. יבמות ס.):

en.t: To whom he is closely related —
to include the betrothed [sister].
Who has not yet been married,
[referring to the marriage’s] consummation.
For her, he may be defiled.
[It is] a [positive] command.

he.t: לא יטמא לאשתו פסולה שהוא מחולל בה בעודה עמו (שם טו. יבמות כב:), וכן פשוטו של מקרא לא יטמא בעל בשארו, בעוד שהיא בתוך עמיו שיש לה קוברין, שאינה מת מצוה, ובאיזה שאר אמרתי, באותו שהיא להחלו, להתחלל הוא מכהונתו:

en.t: A husband may not defile himself among his people to become profaned.

He may not defile himself for an illegitimate wife, through whom he becomes unfit [for the kehunoh], while she is still with him. And thus the plain meaning of the verse is [as follows]: “A husband may not defile himself” — “with his flesh,” while [the corpse is] yet “among his people” — when there are [people available who can] bury her, [that is,] she is not a mes mitzvoh. And regarding what flesh [= wife] did I speak? Regarding one [through] which “he becomes profaned” — to become unfit from his kehunoh.

he.t: על מת, והלא אף ישראל הוזהרו על כך, אלא לפי שנאמר בישראל בין עיניכם, (דברים יד, א) יכול לא יהא חייב על כל הראש, תלמוד לומר בראשם, וילמדו ישראל מהכהנים בגזרה שוה, נאמר כאן קרחה ונאמר להלן בישראל קרחה, מה כאן כל הראש אף להלן כל הראש במשמע, כל מקום שיקרח בראש, ומה להלן על מת, אף כאן על מת (ת"כ פרק א, ג. — קידושין לו. מכות כ.):

en.t: They shall not make baldness

for a deceased person. Were not Israelites also prohibited such [conduct]? However, because it was stated regarding Israelites: “[You shall not make any baldness] ’between your eyes’ [for the dead],” Perhaps he is not liable [for plucking out hair] on [any part] of the head [other than “between the eyes”]? The verse says: “on their head” — and [the law of] Israelites is derived from [the law] of kohanim by [means of] a gezeroh shovoh: “baldness” (קָרְחָה) is mentioned here and “baldness’ (קָרְחָה) is mentioned regarding Israelites — just as here [any part of] the entire head [is implied], so too further on the entire head is implied, wherever he makes a bald spot on the head. And just as further on [the prohibition involves mourning] for a deceased person, so, here [mourning] for a deceased person [is implied].

he.t: לפי שנאמר בישראל ולא תשחית (ויקרא יט, כז), יכול לקטו בְּמַלְקֵט וּרְהִיטָנִי יהא חייב, לכך נאמר לא יגלחו, שאינו חייב אלא על דבר הקרוי גלוח ויש בו השחתה וזהו תער:

en.t: And the corners of their beards they shall not shave.

Because regarding an Israelite it is said, “you shall not destroy [by shaving the corner of your beard],” perhaps for plucking with a tweezer or with plane-like tools he is liable? Therefore it is said, “they shall not shave” — he is liable only for something which is called “shaving” and which has in it “destructiveness,” and that [is accomplished only with] a razor.

he.t: לפי שנאמר בישראל (מכות כא.) וְשֶׂרֶט לָנֶפֶשׁ לֹא תִתְּנוּ (שם כח.), יכול שרט חמש שריטות לא יהא חייב אלא אחת, תלמוד לומר לא ישרטו שרטת, לחייב על כל שריטה ושריטה, שתיבה זו יתירה היא לדרוש, שהיה לו לכתוב לא ישרטו ואני יודע שהיא שרטת:

en.t: They shall not make gashes in their flesh.

Because it is said regarding an [ordinary] Israelite, “A gash for the dead shall you not make,” perhaps [this means that if he] made five gashes, he is liable for only one? The verse says: “They shall not make gashes” — to make him liable for each and every gash. for this word [= “gashes”] is superfluous [and intended] for midrashic exposition, for it should have been written: “They shall not gash,” and I would know that [the verb “gash” refers to] gashes.

he.t: על כרחם יקדישום בית דין בכך (ת"כ פרק א, ו):

en.t: They shall be holy.
The court shall sanctify them against their will in this.

he.t: שנבעלה בעילת ישראל האסור לה, כגון חייבי כריתות או נתין או ממזר (יבמות סא:):

en.t: A harlot,
[A woman] who has had sexual relations with an Israelite who is forbidden for her to marry, under the penalty of koreis [for doing so], or a נָתִין, or a מַמְזֵר .

he.t: שנולדה מן הפסולים שבכהונה, כגון בת אלמנה מכהן גדול, או בת גרושה וחלוצה מכהן הדיוט, וכן שנתחללה מן הכהונה על ידי ביאת אחד מן הפסולים לכהונה (קידושין עז.):

en.t: A profaned woman,

[that is, a woman] who was born of a marriage [between a kohein] and one [forbidden] to the kehunoh, as for example the daughter of a widow [illegally married] to a Kohein Godol, or the daughter of a divorced woman [illegally married] to an ordinary kohein. So too one who became invalid [for intermarriage] with the kehunoh because she had sexual relations in one of the marriages forbidden to a kohein.

he.t: על כרחו, שאם לא רצה לגרש, הלקהו ויסרהו עד שיגרש (יבמות פח:):

en.t: You shall make him holy —
[even] against his will, for if he does not wish to divorce [his illegal wife], beat him and punish him until he does divorce [her].

he.t: נהוג בו קדושה לפתוח ראשון בכל דבר, ולברך ראשון בסעודה (גיטין נט: — ת"כ):

en.t: He shall be holy unto you,
treat him with sanctity, to take precedence in all matters [of sanctity], and to bless first at a meal.

he.t: כשתחלל על ידי זנות, שהיתה בה זיקת בעל, וזנתה או מן האירוסין או מן הנשואין, ורבותינו נחלקו בדבר (סנהדרין נא.), והכל מודים שלא דבר הכתוב בפנויה:

en.t: Who profanes herself by fornication,

when she becomes profaned through fornication, as when she had [some] marital tie with a husband and fornicated, whether [this tie was through] betrothal or marriage. Our Rabbis disagreed about the matter, [but] all agree that the verse does not speak regarding a free woman.

he.t: חללה ובזתה את כבודו, שאומרים עליו ארור שזו ילד, ארור שזו גדל (שם נב.):

en.t: She profanes her father.
She has profaned and degraded his honor, for they say of him: “Cursed be he that he caused this one to be born; cursed be he that he raised this one”!

he.t: לא יגדל פרע על אבל (ת"כ פרשתא ב, ג), ואיזהו גידול פרע יותר משלשים יום (סנהדרין כב:):

en.t: Shall not let [his hair] grow wild,
it shall not grow wild in mourning. And what is [the measure] of “growing wild”? More than thirty days.
And adjacent to any dead body, etc.
[That is,] in[to] a tent [which is over a] dead body.

he.t: להביא רביעית דם מן המת שמטמא באהל (נזיר לח.):

en.t: Dead body
[literally, “souls of a dead body”] — to include a quarter [of a לוֹג] of blood from a dead body, which causes impurity in a “tent.”

he.t: לא בא אלא להתיר לו מת מצוה (שם מז: — ת"כ שם ד):

en.t: For his father and his mother he shall not become [ritually] impure.
This comes only to permit him [to become impure] for a mes mitzvoh.

he.t: אינו הולך אחר המטה (ת"כ שם ה. — סנהדרין יח). ועוד מכאן למדו רבותינו (שם פד.) שכהן גדול מקריב אונן, וכן משמעו, אף אם מתו אביו ואמו אינו צריך לצאת מן המקדש אלא עובד עבודה:

en.t: He shall not depart from the Sanctuary.

He does not follow the coffin. Furthermore, our Rabbis learned from here that a Kohein Godol may offer [a sacrifice] while he is an onein, and this is its meaning: Even if his father and his mother died, he is not required to leave the Sanctuary, but performs the Temple-service.

he.t: שאינו מחלל בכך את העבודה, שהתיר לו הכתוב, הא כהן הדיוט שעבד אונן חלל:

en.t: And he shall not profane. . .the Sanctuary,

He does not profane the Temple-service with this, since Scripture permitted him [to remain there]; thus, [we learn,] that an ordinary kohein who performs [the Temple-service] while he is an onein does profane [it].
And a profaned woman,
born of [a marriage] forbidden to the kehunoh.

he.t: הא אם נשא אחת מן הפסולות, זרעו הימנה חלל מדין קדושת כהונה:

en.t: He shall not profane his offspring —
thus, if he marries one [of those] women invalid [for marriage with kohanim], his offspring from her is profaned from the status of the holiness of the kehunoh.

he.t: מאכל אלהיו, כל סעודה קרויה לחם, כמו עֲבַד לְחֶם רַב (דניאל ה, א):

en.t: The bread of his God,
“the food” of his God. Every meal is called “food,” as [in the verse] “he made a great feast.”

he.t: כי כל איש אשר בו מום לא יקרב.
אינו דין שיקרב, כמו הַקְרִיבֵהוּ נָא לְפֶחָתֶךָ (מלאכי א, ח):

en.t: For any man who has a blemish shall not approach.
It is not proper that he approach; [the word “approach”] is like [that in the verse] “[If you offer the lame or sick, is it not evil?] Offer it now to your governor; [will he be pleased with you?].”

he.t: שחוטמו שקוע בין שתי העינים, שכוחל שתי עיניו כאחת (בכורות מג:) ì :

en.t: A man with a sunken nose,
[one] whose nose is sunken between the two eyes, [so that] he can paint both his eyes with one stroke.

he.t: שאחד מאיבריו גדול מחבירו, עינו אחת גדולה ועינו אחת קטנה, או שוקו אחת ארוכה מחברתה (שם מ:):

en.t: A man who has disproportionate limbs,
[one who has] one limb larger than the other — one eye large and one eye small, or one thigh is longer than the other.

he.t: שוריציול"ש בלע"ז, שגביני עיניו שערן ארוך ושוכב (שם מג:):

en.t: One with overhanging eyebrows.
Sorzilos in Old French, [denoting one whose] eyebrows — their hair is long and lies [over his face].

he.t: שיש לו בעיניו דוק שקורין טיל"א (שם לח.), כמו הַנּוֹטֶה כַדֹּק (ישעיה מ, כב):

en.t: Or with a cataract,
who has a membrane in his eyes, which is called toyle [in Old French], similar [to the use of the word in the verse]: “Who spreads out [the heavens] like a membrane.”

he.t: דבר המבלבל את העין, כגון חוט לבן הנמשך מן הלבן ופוסק בסירא, שהוא עוגל המקיף את השחור שקוראים פרוניל"א, והחוט הזה פוסק את העוגל ונכנס בשחור. ותרגום תבלול חִילִיז, לשון חלזון, שהוא דומה לתולעת אותו החוט, וכן כינוהו חכמי ישראל במומי הבכור חלזון נחש עֵינָב (שם):

en.t: Or a disarrangement [in the eye],

something which confuses the eye, such as a white streak which stretches from the white [of the eye] and intersects the iris — the circle which surrounds the black [of the eye], [that] which is called prunelle in Old French. This streak intersects the circle and enters the black [of the eye]. The Targum of תְּבַלוּל is חִילִּיז, a word [related to] חִלָּזוֹן, for that streak is similar to a worm, and so the Sages of Israel termed it, [when describing] the blemishes [which can befall] a firstling: worm, snake, wart.

he.t: זו החרס, שחין היבש מבפנים ומבחוץ:

היא חזזית המצרית, ולמה נקראת ילפת, שמלפפת והולכת עד יום המיתה, והוא לח מבחוץ ויבש מבפנים. ובמקום אחר קורא לגרב שחין הלח מבחוץ ויבש מבפנים, שנאמר וּבַגָּרָב וּבֶחָרֶס (דברים כח, כז), כשסמוך גרב אצל חרס קורא לילפת גרב, וכשהוא סמוך אצל ילפת קורא לחרס גרב, כך מפורש בבכורות (בכורות מא.):

en.t: Scurf [= gorov] or scabs [= yallefes].

These are types of boils. “Scurf” is [what is called elsewhere] cheres, a boil [which is] dry within and without [on the surface]; “scab” is the Egyptian lichen. And why is it called yallefes? Because it continues to cling [to the body] until the day of death, and it is moist without and dry within, and in another place gorov is called shechin — moist without and dry within, as it is said, “and with the scab [= gorov] and with the itch [= cheres].” When [the word] “scurf” [= gorov] [appears] near cheres, [then] “scab” [= yallefes] is called “scurf” [= gorov], [but] when it [= gorov] [appears] near “scab” [= yallefes], cheres is called “scurf” [= gorov] — so is it explained in Bechoros.

he.t: לפי התרגום מְרִיס פַחֲדִין, שפחדיו מרוססים, שביצים שלו כתותין. פחדין כמו גִידֵי פַחֲדָו יְשֹׂרָגוּ (איוב מ, יז):

en.t: Or one with crushed testicles,

[which is,] according to the Targum: מְרֵס פַּחֲדִין, whose פַּחֲדִין are מְרוּסָסִין — his testicles are crushed. [The word] פַּחֲדִין is related [to its meaning in the verse]: “All the sinews of his testicles are knit together.”

he.t: לרבות שאר מומין (ת"כ פרק ג, א):

en.t: Any man who has a blemish —
[this comes] to include other blemishes.

he.t: בעוד מומו בו פסול, הא אם עבר מומו כשר:

en.t: He has a blemish,
while “he has a blemish,” he is unfit; therefore, if the blemish passes, he is fit.
The bread of his God,
every food is called “bread.”
Of the most holy [sacrifices] —
these are the most holy sacrifices.

he.t: אלו קדשים קלים, ואם נאמרו קדשי הקדשים, למה נאמרו קדשים קלים, אם לא נאמר הייתי אומר בקדשי הקדשים יאכל בעל מום, שמצינו שהותרו לזר, שאכל משה בשר המלואים, אבל בחזה ושוק של קדשים קלים לא יאכל, שלא מצינו זר חולק בהן, לכך נאמרו קדשים קלים (ת"כ פרק ג, ח), כך מפורש בזבחים (קא:):

en.t: And from the holy, he may eat.

These are the sacrifices of lesser sanctity. If sacrifices of greater sanctity are mentioned, why are sacrifices of lesser sanctity [also] mentioned? If it had not been said, I would have thought: A blemished person may eat of the most holy sacrifices, since we find that they were permitted to a non-kohein, [as when] Moshe ate the flesh of the installation-sacrifices. But [I might think] that of the breast and thigh of sacrifices of lesser sanctity he may not eat, since we do not find that a non-kohein had a part in them — therefore sacrifices of lesser sanctity are mentioned. So is it explained in [the Maseches of] Zevochim.
However, [he may not enter] beyond the curtain,
to sprinkle seven sprinklings on the curtain.

he.t: החיצון. ושניהם הוצרכו להכתב, ומפורש בת"כ (שם י.):

en.t: And to the altar,
the outer [one]. And both [the curtain and the altar] had to be written, and [the reason] is explained in Toras Kohanim.
He shall not profane My holy things.
For if he did perform [the service], his service is profaned and becomes invalid.
Moshe spoke
this mitzvah.

he.t: אל אהרן וגו' ואל כל בני ישראל.
להזהיר בית דין על הכהנים (שם יב.).

en.t: To Aharon and to his sons and to all of Bnei Yisroel —
to warn the court regarding the kohanim.

he.t: אין נזירה אלא פרישה, וכן הוא אומר וַיִּנָּזֵר מֵאַחֲרַי (יחזקאל יד, ז), נָזֹרוּ אָחוֹר (ישעיה א, ד), יפרשו מן הקדשים בימי טומאתן. דבר אחר וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל, אשר הם מקדישים לי ולא יחללו את שם קדשי, סרס המקרא ודרשהו:

en.t: And let them keep away,

[The word] נְזִירָה refers to “separation,” and so too [the verse] says: “And he separates himself from following Me,” “They are gone away backward,” [thus implying here:] they shall separate [themselves] from holy things in the days of their impurity. And let them keep away from the holy offerings of Bnei Yisroel, which they sanctify for Me, and not profane My Holy Name. Reverse the verse and expound it.
Which they sanctify for Me,
[this redundancy comes] to include the holy offerings of the kohanim themselves.

he.t: אין קריבה זו אלא אכילה, וכן מצינו שנאמרה אזהרת אכילת קדשים בטומאה בלשון נגיעה, בכל קדש לא תגע, (ויקרא יב, ד) אזהרה לאוכל, ולמדוה רבותינו (זבחים לג:) מגזירה שוה. ואי אפשר לומר שחייב על הנגיעה, שהרי נאמר כרת על האכילה בצו את אהרן שתי כריתות זו אצל זו, ואם על הנגיעה חייב לא הוצרך לחייבו על האכילה, וכן נדרש בת"כ (פרשתא ד, ז), וכי יש נוגע חייב, אם כן מה תלמוד לומר יקרב, משיכשר להקרב, שאין חייבין עליו משום טומאה, אלא אם כן קרבו מתיריו, ואם תאמר שלש כריתות בטומאת כהנים למה, כבר נדרשו במס' שבועות (ז.) אחת לכלל, ואחת לפרט וכו':

en.t: Any person who shall draw near.

This [expression of] “drawing near” refers to eating, and so we have found that the prohibition of eating holy flesh while [in a state of ritual] uncleanness is expressed by [a word implying] “touching”: “Anything holy she shall not touch” — which is a prohibition for one who eats [the flesh], and our Rabbis derived it from a gezeroh shovoh. And it is impossible to say that he is liable for touching, since koreis is mentioned regarding eating in [the Sidroh] of Tzav es Aharon: Two kerisos are [mentioned] next to one another, and if he is liable for touching, it would not have been necessary to make him liable for eating± so is it expounded in Toras Kohanim: Is then a kohein who [merely] touches [sacrificial flesh when he is unclean] liable [to koreis]? If so, why does the verse say: “who draws near” [rather than “who eats”]? [It is said in order to teach that] once it is fit to be offered [= brought near], they [= those who eat it] are not liable for uncleanness unless that which makes it permissible is offered. And if you say: Why are three kerisos regarding impurity of kohanim? [They] were already expounded in Maseches Shevu’os: One is [to teach] a general rule [regarding all sacrifices], one [teaches the rule regarding] a particular case, etc. [and one to teach regarding a sliding-scale sacrifice, which is recorded only to prescribe atonement for the uncleanness of the Temple and its holy food].

he.t: וטומאת האדם עליו. יכול בבשר הכתוב מדבר וטומאתו של בשר עליו, ובטהור שאכל את הטמא הכתוב מדבר, על כרחך ממשמעו אתה למד, במי שטומאתו פורחת ממנו הכתוב מדבר, וזהו האדם שיש לו טהרה בטבילה (זבחים מג:):

en.t: While his impurity is on him —

and the impurity of a human being is on him. Perhaps the verse speaks of the impurity of flesh — “and the impurity of the [sacrificial] flesh is on it”? — And regarding a clean [kohein] who ate unclean [flesh], does scripture speak? [No.] You are forced to learn from what is implied in it. Of one whose impurity passes away from him, does the verse speak. And this refers to a human being whose purification is by immersion.

he.t: יכול מצד זה לצד זה, יכרת ממקומו ויתיישב במקום אחר, תלמוד לומר אני ה', בכל מקום אני:

en.t: Shall be cut off.

Perhaps [he shall be uprooted] from this side [of the world] to the [other] side [of the world]? [Perhaps] he will be cut off [= exiled] from his [native] place and be settled in another place? The verse says:
“I am Adonoy” —
[he will be cut off] from wherever I am.
Anything defiled by the dead,
[referring] to one who becomes [ritually] impure by [contact] with the dead.

he.t: בשיעור הראוי לטמא (ת"כ פרק ד, ד), בכעדשה (חגיגה יא. — ת"כ):

en.t: Any creeping creature that causes impurity to him,
in the minimum size which is capable of causing impurity, [that is, the size of] a lentil.
Or any person,
a dead body.
Who causes impurity to him,
in [the] minimum size to cause impurity, and that is [the volume of] an olive’s-bulk.

he.t: לרבות נוגע בזב, וזבה, נדה, ויולדת:

en.t: [With] whatever impurity he has,
this includes one who touches a zov, or a zovoh, or a niddoh, or a woman who has just given birth.
Anyone touching [that person] —
any of these [ritually] unclean [persons].

he.t: נדרש ביבמות (עד:) בתרומה, שמותר לאכלה בהערב השמש:

en.t: And afterwards, he may eat of the holy things.
[This] is expounded in [Maseches] Yevomos [as concerning] terumoh, which [kohanim] are permitted to eat at sunset.
Of the holy things.
but not all the holy things.

he.t: נבלה וטרפה לא יאכל לטמאה בה.
לענין הטומאה הזהיר כאן, שאם אכל נבלת עוף טהור שאין לה טומאת מגע ומשא, אלא טומאת אכילה בבית הבליעה, אסור לאכול בקדשים, וצריך לומר וטרפה, מי שיש במינו טרפה, יצא נבלת עוף טמא שאין במינו טרפה:

en.t: An animal which has died on its own, or an animal that was fatally maimed, he must not eat to defile himself with it.

[This verse] warns regarding the matter of uncleanness. That if he ate the carcass of a [ritually] clean bird, which has no [rule of] uncleanness of touch and carrying, except for the uncleanness [caused by] eating as soon as it is in the gullet — he is forbidden to eat holy things. [Furthermore,] it was necessary to state u’trefah, [to indicate that the word neveiloh] [refers to] an animal whose species includes a trefah — excluding the carcass of an unclean bird which does not include a trefah within its species.
They shall keep My charge
not to eat terumoh while [in a state of] bodily uncleanness.

he.t: למדנו שהיא מיתה בידי שמים (סנהדרין פג.):

en.t: And die because of it.
This has taught us that [violation of this prohibition] is [punishable] by death at the hands of Heaven.

he.t: בתרומה הכתוב מדבר, שכל הענין דבר בה (שם פג:):

en.t: No stranger (non-kohein) may eat holy things.
The verse speaks of terumoh, for the whole passage speaks of it.

he.t: תושבו של כהן ושכירו, לפיכך תושב זה נקוד פתח, לפי שהוא דבוק, ואיזהו תושב, זה נרצע שהוא קנוי לו עד היובל, ואיזהו שכיר, זה קנוי קנין שנים שיוצא בשש, בא הכתוב ולמדך כאן, שאין גופו קנוי לאדוניו לאכול בתרומתו (יבמות ע.):

en.t: One indentured to a kohein or one hired —

[that is,] the indentured servant of a kohein or his hired hand. That is why [the word] “ תּוֹשַׁב “ is vocalized with a פַּתַּח, because it is connected [to the following word]. And what is a תּוֹשָׁב ? This is [a Hebrew servant] who [has had his ear] pierced, who belongs [to his master] until the Jubilee year. And what is a שָׂכִיר ? One who belongs [to his master] for [a period] of years, who leaves [his master’s service] in six years. The verse has come and taught you here, that he does not belong bodily to his master [which would allow him to] eat terumoh.
If a kohein shall purchase a person [as a slave],
a Canaanite slave who belongs bodily [to his master].

he.t: אלו בני השפחות, ואשת כהן אוכלת בתרומה מן המקרא הזה, שאף היא קנין כספו (כתובות נז:), ועוד למד ממקרא אחר כל טהור בביתך וגו' בספרי (קרח יז):

en.t: And the [slave] born in his house,

these are the children of the maidservants. [Furthermore, the law that] the wife of a kohein may eat terumoh [is derived] from this verse, for she too is an acquisition obtained with his money. and [this law] is also learned from another verse: “Every [ritually] clean person in your house [may eat of it]” — in Sifrei.
To a non-kohein,
[that is,] to a Levite or an Israelite.
Widowed or divorced —
from the non-kohein.
And she has no children
from him.

he.t: הא אם יש לה זרע ממנו, אסורה בתרומה כל זמן שהזרע קיים (יבמות פז.):

en.t: And she returns —
therefore, if she has children from him, she is forbidden [to eat] terumoh as long as the children live.

he.t: לא בא אלא להוציא את האונן שמותר בתרומה, זרות אמרתי לך, ולא אנינות (שם סח:):

en.t: No non-kohein may eat of it,
[this repetition] comes only to exclude an onein [from the prohibition] — for he is permitted [to eat] terumoh. I said to you: A non-kohein [is forbidden to eat terumoh], but not an onein.
If a man eats of holy things —
terumah.

he.t: דבר הראוי להיות קדש, שאינו פורע לו מעות, אלא פירות של חולין, והן נעשין תרומה (פסחים לב.):

en.t: And give to the kohein the holy thing.
Something which is fit to become holy — that he not pay him in coin, but in common [i.e., non-holy] produce, which becomes terumoh.
They shall not profane, etc.
To feed them to strangers.

he.t: את עצמם יטענו עון באכלם את קדשיהם, שהובדלו לשם תרומה וקדשו, ונאסרו עליהם. ואונקלוס שתרגם בְּמֵיכָלְהוֹן בְּסוֹאֲבָא, שלא לצורך תרגמו כן:

en.t: They burden them[selves]
[they] themselves will bear the sin —
when they eat their holy things,

that were separated for the sake of terumoh and became holy and were forbidden to them [= the strangers]. And Onkelos who translated “in their eating [of it] in impurity,” translated it thus unnecessarily.

he.t: זה אחד מג' אתים שהיה רבי ישמעאל דורש בתורה שמדברים באדם עצמו, וכן בְּיוֹם מְלֹאת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ יָבִיא אֹתוֹ (במדבר ו, יג), הוא יביא את עצמו, וכן וַיִּקְבֹּר אֹתוֹ בַגַּיא (דברים לד, ו), הוא קבר את עצמו, כך נדרש בספרי (נשא לב):

en.t: They burden them[selves].

This is one of three [mentions of the word] es in the Torah which R. Yishmo’el would expound [as though the verses] were speaking of the person himself; and so [too]: “on the day in which the time of his nezirus is fulfilled, he shall bring him” — he shall bring himself; and so [too]: “and he buried him in the valley” — he buried himself. So is it expounded in Sifre.
Vows —
[he says:] “I am obligated [to bring this sacrifice].”
Free-will-offerings,
[he says:] “Behold, this [I will bring].”

he.t: הביאו דבר הראוי לרצות אתכם לפני, שיהא לכם לרצון, אפיישמנ"ט בלע"ז. ואיזהו הראוי לרצון:

en.t: To gain acceptance —
bring something fit to ingratiate yourselves before Me, that [the offering] should be acceptable for you, apayement in Old French. And what is fitting for acceptance?

he.t: אבל בעולת העוף אין צריך תמות וזכרות, ואינו נפסל במום, אלא בחסרון אבר:

en.t: An unblemished male of cattle, sheep or goats.
But a bird burnt-offering does not require an unblemished state and masculinity, and is not invalidated by a blemish, but [rather] by loss of a limb.
To fulfill an articulated vow,
to express [clearly] by his speech.

he.t: שם דבר של מום, עִוָּרוֹן בלשון נקבה, שלא יהא בו מום של עורת:

en.t: Blind,
[this is] the noun [denoting] the blemish, “blindness” in a feminine form. It shall not have the blemish of blindness.
Or broken-limbed
it shall not be.

he.t: ריס של עין שנסדק או שנפגם (בכורות לח.), וכן שפתו שנסדקה או נפגמה (שם לט.):

en.t: Or cracked,
an eye-lid which is split or nipped, and so [too if] its lip is split or nipped.
Wart.
Verue in Old French.

he.t: מין חזזית, וכן ילפת ולשון ילפת כמו וַיִּלְפֹּת שִׁמְשׁוֹן (שופטים טז, כט), שאחוזה בו עד יום מיתה, שאין לה רפואה (בכורות מא.):

en.t: Scurf,

a type of lichen and so [too] scab, and the expression of “scab” is like [= related to] “And Samson took hold [of the two middle pillars].” [It is so called because] it keeps its hold on him [= the sick peron] to the day of his death, for it has no cure.

he.t: שלש פעמים, להזהיר על הקדשתן, ועל שחיטתן, ועל זריקת דמן (תמורה ו:):

en.t: You shall not bring —
[this is mentioned] three times, [once] to forbid its designation [as an offering], [once to forbid] its slaughter, [and once to forbid] the sprinkling of its blood.
And as a fire-offering you shall not place —
a prohibition [against] burning them [on the altar].
Soru’o.
[where] one limb is larger than the other.
Or kolut.
[an animal] whose hooves are uncloven.
You shall make it as a free-will-offering —
for the repair of the Temple.
[But] for [the fulfillment of] a vow —
for the altar,

he.t: איזה הקדש בא לרצות, הוי אומר זה הקדש המזבח (ת"כ פרק ז, ו):

en.t: it will not be favorably accepted.
What dedicated thing comes to gain acceptance? Say: this is the dedicated [animal intended] for the altar.
And crushed, mangled, torn or cut off —
[referring to the animal’s] testicles or organ.
Crushed,
its testicles are crushed by hand.
Mangled,
cut off to a greater extent [than the cutting described] by “crushed.”

he.t: תלושין ביד עד שנפסקו חוטים שתלויים בהן, אבל נתונים הם בתוך הכיס, והכיס לא נתלש:

en.t: Torn,
torn by hand until the threads by which they hang are separated, but they are still in the pouch, and the pouch is not cut off.
Cut off,
cut off with an instrument, but they are still in the pouch.

he.t: תרגומו וְדִמְרִיס, זה לשונו בארמית, לשון כתישה:

en.t: And crushed,
its Targum is “and which is bruised,” this is its meaning in Aramaic — an expression of “crushing.”

he.t: תרגומו וְדִרְסִיס, כמו הַבַּיִת הַגָּדוֹל רְסִיסִים (עמוס ו, יא), בְּקִיעוֹת דַּקּוֹת, וכן קנה המרוסס (שבת פ:):

en.t: And mangled,

its Targum is “and which is smashed,” as [in the verse]: “The great house shall be smitten into fragments” — into small pieces, and so [too in the Talmudic expression]: “a reed broken into small pieces.”

he.t: דבר זה לסרס שום בהמה וחיה ואפילו טמאה, לכך נאמר בארצכם, לרבות כל אשר בארצכם, שאי אפשר לומר לא נצטוו על הסרוס אלא בארץ, שהרי סרוס חובת הגוף הוא, וכל חובת הגוף נוהגת בין בארץ בין בחוצה לארץ (קידושין לו:):

en.t: In your land shall you not do

this thing, to castrate any animal or beast, even a [ritually] unclean one — therefore it is said, “in your land,” to include all that is in your land, for it is impossible to say that they were commanded regarding castration only in the land [of Israel], for [the prohibition of] castration is an obligation [pertaining to] the person, and every obligation [pertaining to] the person applies both in the land and outside the land.

he.t: נכרי שהביא קרבן ביד כהן להקריבו לשמים.

לו בעל מום, ואף על פי שלא נאסרו בעלי מומים לקרבן בני נח אלא אם כן מחוסרי אבר, זאת נוהגת בבמה שבשדות, (תמורה ז.) אבל על המזבח שבמשכן לא תקריבוה, אבל תמימה תקבלו מהם, לכך נאמר למעלה (פסוק יח) איש איש, לרבות את הנכרים שנודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל (חולין יג:):

en.t: From a stranger’s hand [you shall not bring],
that he brought a sacrifice by the hand of a kohein, to offer it to Heaven.
You shall not bring

on his behalf a blemished [animal]. And even though blemished [animals] were not forbidden as an offering from the sons of Noach, except if they were missing a limb, this applies only to altars in the fields, but [animals brought] on the altar of the Tabernacle you should not bring, though unblemished [offerings] you may accept from them. Therefore it was said above: “Any man” — to include non-Jews who may make vows and bring free-will-offerings as [do] Israelites.
Wounds,
wounds, (quoting Targum).
They will not be favorably accepted for you,
to atone for you.
When it is born,
excluding a Caesarian section.

he.t: נוהג בנקבה, שאסור לשחוט האם והבן או הבת, ואינו נוהג בזכרים, ומותר לשחוט האב והבן (ת"כ פרק ח, א — חולין עח:):

en.t: It and its offspring.

[This rule] applies to a female [animal], for it is forbidden to slaughter the mother [together with] the son or daughter [on the same day]. It does not apply to male [animals], and it is permitted to slaughter the father and the son.
It and its offspring,
even its offspring and it are implied [in the expression].

he.t: תחלת זביחתכם הזהרו שתהא לרצון לכם, ומהו הרצון:

en.t: That it be favorably accepted for you shall you sacrifice it.
[That is, at] the outset of its slaughtering, be careful that it should bring acceptance for you, and what is it that assures its acceptance?

he.t: לא בא להזהיר אלא שתהא שחיטה על מנת כן, אל תשחוטוהו על מנת לאכלו למחר, שאם תחשבו בו מחשבת פסול לא יהא לכם לרצון. דבר אחר לרצונכם, לדעתכם, מכאן למתעסק שפסול בשחיטת קדשים (חולין יג.), ואף על פי שפרט בנאכלים לשני ימים, חזר ופרט בנאכלין ליום אחד, שתהא זביחתן על מנת לאכלן בזמנן:
לא בא להזהיר אלא שתהא שחיטה על מנת כן, שאם לקבוע לה זמן אכילה, כבר כתיב וּבְשַׂר זֶבַח תּוֹדַת שְׁלָמָיו וגו' (ויקרא ז, טו):

en.t: On that day [that it is sacrificed] it may be eaten.

This comes to warn that the slaughtering should be for this purpose — do not slaughter it in order to eat it tomorrow, for if you have invalidating thoughts, it will not be acceptable for you. Another interpretation:
That it be favorably accepted for you —

consciously; from here [we learn] that one who is preoccupied [and in this state slaughters an offering], it is invalid in regard to the slaughter of holy offerings. And even though it detailed [this rule] in regard to [sacrifices] eaten for two days [and the night between], [the verse] again detailed [it here], regarding [those] eaten for one day — that their slaughter should be with the intention to eat them in their [proper] time.
On that day [that it is sacrificed] you should eat it.

This comes only to warn that the slaughter should be for this purpose, for if [it comes] to set a time of eating, [that] was already written: “The flesh of his peace-offering for thanksgiving [shall be eaten on the day of his offering].”

he.t: דע מי גזר על הדבר ואל יקל בעיניך:

en.t: I am Adonoy.
Know Who decrees [this] thing, and let it not be trivial in your eyes.
You shall preserve —
this [refers] to study.
And fulfill —
this [refers] to action.

he.t: לעבור על דְּבָרַי מְזִידִין. ממשמע שנאמר ולא תחללו, מה תלמוד לומר ונקדשתי, מסור עצמך וקדש שמי, יכול ביחיד, תלמוד לומר בתוך בני ישראל, וכשהוא מוסר עצמו ימסור עצמו על מנת למות, שכל המוסר עצמו על מנת הנס, אין עושין לו נס, שכן מצינו בחנניה מישאל ועזריה שלא מסרו עצמן על מנת הנס שנאמר וְהֵן לָא יְדִיעַ לֶהֱוֵא לָךְ מַלְכָּא וגו' (דניאל ג, יח), מציל ולא מציל ידיע להוי לך וגו':

en.t: You shall not profane,

to transgress My words intentionally. Since it is said, “and you shall not profane,” why does the verse say, “and I will be sanctified”? Surrender yourself [to martyrdom] and sanctify My Name! Perhaps [this command applies even when] he is alone? The verse says:
Among Bnei Yisroel.

And when he surrenders himself, he should surrender himself in order to die, for whoever surrenders himself [to martyrdom] for the sake of a miracle, a miracle is not performed for him. For so we find in [the case of] Chananiyoh, Misho’el and Azariyoh, who did not surrender themselves for the sake of a miracle, as it is said, “But if not [= if He does not save us], be it known to you, o King, [that we will not serve your gods], etc.” — whether He saves [us] or whether he does not save [us], it should be known to you, etc. [= that we will not serve your idols]
Who brought you out —
for this purpose.
I am Adonoy,
faithful to give reward.

he.t: דבר אל בני ישראל וגו' מועדי ה'.
עשה מועדות שיהיו ישראל מלומדין בהם, שמעברים את השנה על גליות שנעקרו ממקומם לעלות לרגל ועדיין לא הגיעו לירושלים:

en.t: Speak to Bnei Yisroel, [and say to them], the appointed times.

Regulate the appointed times so that [the] Israel[ites] should become practiced in them. [We learn from this] that [the Sanhedrin] proclaims a leap year for those living in the Exile who have left their homes to ascend [to Jerusalem] for the festival, [but] have not yet reached Jerusalem.

he.t: מה ענין שבת אצל מועדות, ללמדך שכל המחלל את המועדות, מעלין עליו כאילו חלל את השבתות, וכל המקיים את המועדות, מעלין עליו כאלו קיים את השבתות:

en.t: Six days.

What is the connection between Shabbos and the festivals? To teach you that whoever profanes the festivals is considered as though he profaned the Shabbasos, and whoever keeps the festivals is considered as though he kept the Shabbasos.

he.t: למעלה מדבר בְּעִבּוּר שָׁנָה וכאן מדבר בקדוש החדש:

en.t: These are the appointed times of Adonoy.
Above [the verse] speaks of proclaiming a leap year, and here it speaks of sanctification of the month.
In the afternoon,
from six hours onward.
A Pesach (offering) for Adonoy,
[referring] to bringing the sacrifice whose name is Pesach.

he.t: הם המוספין האמורים בפרשת פנחס, ולמה נאמרו כאן, לומר לך שאין המוספין מעכבין זה את זה (מנחות מט.):

en.t: You shall bring a fire-offering, etc.
These are the additional sacrifices which are mentioned in Parshas Pinchos. And why are they mentioned here? To say that the[se] additional sacrifices do not impede one another, [since it states]:

he.t: מכל מקום, אם אין פרים, הָבֵא אילים, ואם אין פרים ואילים, הָבֵא כבשים:

en.t: You shall bring a fire-offering to Adonoy,
[bring it] under any circumstance if there are no oxen [available], bring rams, and if there are no oxen or rams, bring lambs.

he.t: כל מקום שנאמר שבעת, שם דבר הוא שבוע של ימים, שטיינ"א בלע"ז, וכן כל לשון שמונת, ששת, חמשת, שלשת:

en.t: [On each of] seven days.
Wherever שִׁבְעַת, (“seven”) is said, it is a noun — a week of days, seteyne in Old French, and so too every expression of “eight of,” “six of.” “five of,” “three of.”

he.t: אפילו מלאכות החשובות לכם עבודה וצורך שיש חסרון כיס בבטלה שלהן, כגון דבר האבד, כך הבנתי מתורת כהנים (פרשתא יב, ח), דקתני יכול אף חולו של מועד יהא אסור במלאכת עבודה וכו':

en.t: You shall not do any work of labor.

Even that work which is considered as necessary labor, which cause[s] monetary loss by its neglect, such as an opportunity which is lost. So have I understood from Toras Kohanim, which teaches: “Perhaps even [during] the intermediate days of the festival the work of labor should be forbidden? Etc.
First fruits of your harvest —
that it should be the first of the harvest.

he.t: עשירית האיפה, כך היתה שמה, כמו וַיָּמֹדּוּ בָעֹמֶר (שמות טז, יח):

en.t: An omer,
a tenth of an ephoh — such was its name, as: “[when] they measured [it] by the omer.”

he.t: כל תנופה מוליך ומביא מעלה ומוריד, מוליך ומביא לעצור רוחות רעות, מעלה ומוריד לעצור טללים רעים (מנחות סב.):

en.t: He shall wave.

Every waving [denotes that] he moves [it] horizontally away from him and toward him, vertically upwards and downwards; horizontally away from him and toward him — to prevent destructive winds, [and] vertically upwards and downwards — to prevent harmful dews.

he.t: אם תקריבו כמשפט זה יהיה לרצון לכם:

en.t: Be favorably accepted for you.
If you bring [it] according to this rule, it will be favorably accepted for you.

he.t: ממחרת יום טוב הראשון של פסח, שאם אתה אומר שבת בראשית אי אתה יודע איזהו (שם סו.):

en.t: On the day after the day of rest,
the day after the first festival day of Pesach, for if you say that [this refers] to the Shabbos of Creation, you [cannot] know which [Shabbos] is meant.
You shall prepare. . .a lamb,
[which] comes as an obligation in connection with the omer [meal-offering].
Its meal-offering,
the meal-offering [which accompanies] its wine-offering.
Two tenths —
it was double.

he.t: אף על פי שמנחתו כפולה, אין נסכיו כפולים (מנחות פט:):

en.t: Its wine-offering is one fourth of a hin.
Even though its meal-offering was double, its wine-offering was not double.

he.t: קמח עשוי מכרמל רך שמייבשין אותו בתנור:

en.t: Parched grain,
flour made from tender grain, which is dried in an oven.
Tender grain,
those are the parched grains, which are called greneds [in Old French].

he.t: נחלקו בו חכמי ישראל (קידושין לז.), יש שלמדו מכאן, שהחדש נוהג בחוצה לארץ, ויש אומרים, לא בא אלא ללמד שלא נצטוו על החדש אלא לאחר ירושה וישיבה משכבשו וחלקו:

en.t: In all your dwelling places.

The Sages of Israel disagreed about this. Some learned from this that [the prohibition] of חָדָשׁ applies outside the land [of Israel], and some say that this comes only to teach [us] that we were not commanded regarding חָדָשׁ until after taking possession and settling [the land], after conquering and dividing [it among the tribes].
From the day after the day of rest,
the day after the festival.

he.t: מלמד שמתחיל ומונה מבערב, שאם לא כן אינן תמימות (שם סו.):

en.t: Seven complete weeks shall they be.
[This] teaches that one should begin [to] count at night, for if not so, they [= the seven weeks] are not complete.
The seventh week,
as its Targum: “the seventh week.”

he.t: ולא עד בכלל, והן ארבעים ותשעה יום:

en.t: Until the day after the seventh week, you shall count [fifty days].
But not including [the day] until which you count — and those are the forty-nine days [referred to].

he.t: חמשים יום והקרבתם מנחה חדשה לה'.
ביום החמשים תקריבוה. ואומר אני זהו מדרשו, אבל פשוטו עד ממחרת השבת השביעית שהוא יום חמשים תספרו, ומקרא מסורס הוא:

en.t: Fifty days, and you shall bring a new meal-offering for Adonoy.

Bring it on the fiftieth day. I say this is its Midrash, but its plain meaning is: “Until the day after the seventh week — which is the fiftieth day — you should count” [and then bring the offering]. [This] is an inverted verse.

he.t: היא המנחה הראשונה שהובאה מן החדש, ואם תאמר הרי קרבה מנחת העומר, אינה כשאר כל המנחות שהיא באה מן השעורים:

en.t: A new meal-offering.

“That is the first meal-offering which is brought from chodosh, and if you say: “But the omer meal-offering has [already] been brought”! [The omer meal-offering] is not like other meal-offerings, for it comes from barley.
From your dwelling places —
and not from outside the land [of Israel].

he.t: לחם תרומה המורם לשם גבוה, וזו היא המנחה החדשה האמורה למעלה:

en.t: Bread wave-offering,
the bread [to be] raised, which is raised [= offered] for the Most High, and this is the “new meal-offering” mentioned above.

he.t: ראשונה לכל המנחות, אף למנחת קנאות הבאה מן השעורים לא תקרב מן החדש קודם לשתי הלחם (שם פד:):

en.t: First fruit-offering,
first of all the meal-offerings — even of the “jealousy” meal-offering which comes from barley, may not be brought from chodosh before the “two breads.”
Along with the bread,
for the sake of the bread, an obligation of the bread.

he.t: כמשפט מנחה ונסכים המפורשים בכל בהמה בפרשת נסכים, ג' עשרונים לפר, וב' עשרונים לאיל, ועשרון לכבש, זו היא המנחה. והנסכים, חצי ההין לפר, ושלישית ההין לאיל, ורביעית ההין לכבש (במדבר טו, ד־ז ט־י):

en.t: With their meal-offerings and wine-offerings,

according to the rule of meal-offerings and wine-offerings explained regarding every animal [sacrifice] in the poroshoh of wine-offerings: three tenths for each ox and two tenths for each ram, and a tenth for each lamb — this is the meal-offering. [As for] the wine-offerings: half a hin for each ox, a third of a hin for each ram, and a fourth of a hin for each lamb.

he.t: יכול ז' כבשים והשעיר האמורים כאן הם ז' הכבשים והשעיר האמורים בחומש הפקודים, כשאתה מגיע אצל פרים ואילים אינן הם, אמור מעתה אלו לעצמן ואלו לעצמן, אלו קרבו בגלל הלחם ואלו למוספין (ת"כ פרק יג, ו — מנחות מה:):

en.t: You shall prepare one he-goat.

Perhaps the seven lambs and the he-goat mentioned here are identical with the seven lambs and he-goat mentioned in חוּמַּשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים ? When you reach the [listing] of oxen and rams, [you see] that it is not so. You must conclude from this [that] these are [a group] unto themselves and these are [a group] unto themselves. These are brought for the sake of the bread, and these are for the additional sacrifices.

he.t: מלמד שטעונין תנופה מחיים (מנחות סב.), יכול כולם, תלמוד לומר על שני כבשים:

en.t: The kohein shall wave them, a wave-offering.
[This] teaches that they require waving [while] alive. Perhaps all of them? The verse says: “with the two lambs.”

he.t: לפי ששלמי יחיד קדשים קלים, הוזקק לומר בשלמי צבור שהם קדשי קדשים:

en.t: They shall be holy.

Because peace-offerings brought by an individual [are classified] as holy things of a lesser degree, it was necessary to state of communal peace-offerings, that they are holy things of a greater degree.

he.t: חזר ושנה, לעבור עליהם בשני לאוין. אמר רבי אבדימי ברבי יוסף, מה ראה הכתוב ליתנם באמצע הרגלים, פסח ועצרת מכאן, וראש השנה ויום הכפורים וחג מכאן, ללמדך שכל הנותן לקט שכחה ופאה לעני כראוי, מעלין עליו כאילו בנה בית המקדש והקריב קרבנותיו בתוכו:

en.t: When you reap.

[The verse] repeats [the prohibition] so that a transgressor violates two prohibitions. Said R. Avdimi son of R. Yosef: Why did Scripture place it [= this agricultural prohibition] in the midst of the festival [laws], Pesach and Shevu’os on one side, Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Sukkos on the other? [In order] to teach you that whoever gives gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the corner of the field to the poor person [in a] proper [manner], is considered as though he built the Temple and brought his sacrifices within it.

he.t: הנח לפניהם, והם ילקטו ואין לך לסייע לאחד מהם:

en.t: You shall leave,
leave [it] before them and they will gather [it], and you must not help any one of them [in preference to anyone else].
I am Adonoy, your God,
faithful to give a reward.

he.t: זכרון פסוקי זכרונות ופסוקי שופרות (ר"ה לב.), לזכור לכם עקידת יצחק שקרב תחתיו איל:

en.t: A remembrance of the sounding [of the shofor].

A mention of Biblical verses [which relate] to [Divine] Remembrances and Biblical verses [which relate to the] shofor — to remember for your sake the binding of Yitzchok for whom a ram was brought in his stead.
You shall bring a fire-offering,
the additional offerings mentioned in חוּמַשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים .

he.t: כל אכין ורקין שבתורה מיעוטין, מכפר הוא לשבים ואינו מכפר לשאינם שבים (שבועות יג.):

en.t: Indeed.

Every time “however” and “indeed (except),” [are mentioned] in the Torah [they represent] a limitation. [Here, the limitation is this:] [Yom Kippur] atones for those who repent, but does not atone for those who do not repent.

he.t: לפי שהוא אומר כרת בכל מקום ואיני יודע מה הוא, כשהוא אומר והאבדתי, למד על הכרת שאינו אלא אבדן:

en.t: I will cause [that person] to perish.

Because [the verse] says “cutting off” everywhere [else], and I do not know what that is, [here] when it says, “I will cause [that person] to perish” it teaches that koreis is nothing other than destruction.

he.t: לעבור עליו בלאוין הרבה, או להזהיר על מלאכת לילה כמלאכת יום (יומא פא.):

en.t: Any work, etc.
[This is repeated to teach that one who does work on Yom Kippur] transgresses many prohibitions, or to [teach that] work at night is prohibited, just as working during the day [is prohibited].

he.t: [ביוה"כ] קדשהו בכסות נקיה ובתפלה, ובשאר ימים טובים, במאכל ובמשתה ובכסות נקיה ובתפלה:

en.t: A holy assembly.
Sanctify it with fine clothing and with prayer, and in regard to other festivals, [sanctify them] with food, drink, fine clothing and prayer.

he.t: עצרתי אתכם אצלי, כמלך שזימן את בניו לסעודה לכך וכך ימים, כיון שהגיע זמנן להפטר אמר, בני, בבקשה מכם עכבו עמי עוד יום אחד, קשה עלי פרידתכם:

en.t: It is [a day] of convocation.

I have kept you with me, like a king who invited his children for a feast for a certain number of days, when the time came for them to leave, he said: “My children, I beg of you, remain with me one more day; your leaving is difficult for me.”

he.t: אפילו מלאכה שהיא עבודה לכם, שאם לא תעשוה יש חסרון כיס בדבר:

en.t: Any work of labor,
even work which is labor for yourselves, that if you do not do it, there will be a loss [to you] in the matter —

he.t: יכול אף חולו של מועד יהא אסור במלאכת עבודה, תלמוד לומר, היא:

en.t: You shall not do.
Perhaps [this applies to] the intermediate days of the festival, that [all] work or labor should be forbidden? The verse says: “It [is a day of convocation].”

he.t: מנחת נסכים הקריבה עם העולה (מנחות מד:):

en.t: A burnt-offering and a meal-offering,
a meal-offering [which accompanies] the wine-offering which is brought with the burnt-offering.
Each on its assigned day,
a quantity fixed in Chumash Hapekudim.

he.t: הא אם עבר יומו בטל קרבנו:

en.t: Each on its assigned day —
therefore, if the day has passed, the sacrifice is cancelled.

he.t: קרבן שלמים לחגיגה, יכול תדחה את השבת, תלמוד לומר, אך, הואיל ויש לה תשלומין כל שבעה:

en.t: Indeed, on the fifteenth day, you shall celebrate —

[bringing] a peace-offering [as] sacrifice for the pilgrim’s sacrifice. Perhaps this [sacrifice] supersedes Shabbos? The verse says: “However,” [which is a limitation]; since it has [a supplementary period] for repayment all seven [days of the festival].

he.t: שיהא חדש שביעי זה בא בזמן אסיפה, מכאן שנצטוו לְעַבֵּר את השנים שאם אין העבור, פעמים שהוא בא באמצע הקיץ או החורף:

en.t: When you gather the produce of the land —

that this seventh month should come at the time of harvest. From here [we learn] that they were commanded to intercalate the years, for if it were not for this addition of a month, at times [Sukkos would fall] during the middle of the summer or the winter.
You shall celebrate —
peace-offerings for the festival sacrifice.

he.t: אם לא הביא בזה יביא בזה, יכול יהא מביאן כל שבעה, תלמוד לומר וחגותם אותו, יום אחד במשמע, ולא יותר, ולמה נאמר שבעה, לתשלומין (חגיגה ט.):

en.t: Seven days,
if he did not bring [the sacrifice] on one [day], he brings it another [day]. Perhaps he brings them all seven [days]? The verse says:
You shall celebrate it —
one day is meant, and not more. Why [then] is “seven” said? For the [supplementary] payment period.

he.t: עץ, שטעם עצו ופריו שוה (סוכה לה.):

en.t: Fruit of the beautiful tree,
a tree the taste of whose wood and fruit are the same.

he.t: הַדָּר באילנו משנה לשנה, וזהו אתרוג (שם):

en.t: Beautiful,
which remain on its tree from year to year — and this is the אֶתְרג [= citron].

he.t: חסר וי"ו, למד שאינה אלא אחת (שם לב.):

en.t: A branch of palm trees.
[Since the word כַּפּוֹת, “branches” appears] without a vov, this teaches that there is only one [palm branch].

he.t: שענפיו קלועים כעבותות וכחבלים, וזהו הדס, העשוי כמין קליעה (שם לב:):

en.t: Boughs of thick-leaved trees,
whose branches are intertwined like ropes and like cords, and this is the הֲדַס [= myrtle] which is shaped like a braid.

he.t: לרבות את הגרים (שם כח: — ת"כ פרק יז, ט):

en.t: Native born,
this is the native-born, [and so the word]
Israelite
[which follows, is seemingly unnecessary, and comes] to include converts.
That in the sukkos I caused to dwell,
[in] clouds of glory.

he.t: זו פרשת מצות הנרות, ופרשת ואתה תצוה לא נאמרה אלא על סדר מלאכת המשכן, לפרש צורך המנורה, וכן משמע ואתה סופך לצוות את בני ישראל על כך:

en.t: Command Bnei Yisroel.

This is the section concerning the mitzvoh of the [Tabernacle] lamps. And the section in the poroshoh of Ve-Atoh Tetzavveh, was mentioned [there] only for the sake of the Order of the Work of the Tabernacle, to explain the purpose of the menorah, and so it implies: You will in the end command Bnei Yisroel regarding this.

he.t: שלשה שמנים יוצאים מן הזית, הראשון קרוי זך, והן מפורשים במנחות (פו.) ובת"כ (פרשתא יג, א):

en.t: Pure, pressed olive oil.
Three oils come forth from the olive: [the oil of] the first [pressing] is called “pure” — and [these three oils] are explained in [Maseches] Menochos, and Toras Kohanim.

he.t: מלילה ללילה, כמו עולת תמיד (במדבר כח ו), שאינה אלא מיום ליום:

en.t: Continually,
from night to night, like [the expression] “a continual burnt-offering,” which [comes] only from day to day.

he.t: שלפני הארון, שהוא קרוי עדות. ורבותינו דרשו (שבת כב. — ת"כ שם ט), על נר מערבי, שהוא עדות לכל באי עולם, שהשכינה שורה בישראל, שנותן בה שמן כמדת חברותיה, וממנה היה מתחיל, ובה היה מסיים:

en.t: The Curtain of Testimony,

which is before the Ark, which is called “Testimony.” And our Rabbis expounded [this as referring] to the westernmost lamp, which is testimony for all the world’s inhabitants that the Divine Presence dwells in the midst of Israel. [This is because the Kohein Godol] places as much oil in it as for the other lamps, [but] from it he would begin [to light the lamps] and with it he would end.

he.t: יערוך אתו אהרן מערב עד בוקר.
יערוך אותו, עריכה הראויה למדת כל הלילה (ת"כ שם יא), ושיערו חכמים, חצי לוג לכל נר ונר, והן כדאי אף ללילי תקופת טבת, ומדה זו הוקבעה להם (מנחות פט.):

en.t: Aharon shall arrange it [so that it burns] from evening until morning.

He should arrange it in a suitable arrangement according to the length of each night; the Sages estimated [this] at half a log for each lamp, and this was fit for even the [long] nights of the Teves season, and this measure was set for them [for the entire year].

he.t: שהיא זהב טהור. דבר אחר על טהרה של מנורה, שמטהרה ומדשנה תחלה מן האפר:

en.t: The pure menorah,
[that is, the menorah] which is [made of] pure gold. Another interpretation: [He should arrange the lamps] on the purity of the menorah, [by] first purifying it and cleaning it of its ashes.
Six in each stack —
six loaves in one stack.

he.t: של זהב טהור. דבר אחר על טהרו של שלחן, שלא יהיו הסניפין מגביהין את הלחם מעל גבי השלחן (ת"כ פרק יח, ד):

en.t: The pure table,

[that is, the table made] of pure gold. Another interpretation: [The loaves should be placed] on the “purity” of the table, that the supportsshould not raise the [lowest loaves of] bread above the table.

he.t: על כל אחת משתי המערכות, היו שני בזיכי לבונה, מלא קומץ לכל אחת:

en.t: You shall put on [each] stack,
on each one of the two stacks; there were two bowls of frankincense [in all], a fistful [of frankincense] for each one [= bowl].
And it shall be —
this frankincense,

he.t: שאין מן הלחם לגבוה כלום, אלא הלבונה נקטרת כשמסלקין אותו בכל שבת ושבת, והיא לזכרון ללחם, שעל ידה הוא נזכר למעלה כקומץ, שהוא אזכרה למנחה:

en.t: as a memorial portion for the bread,

because of the bread itself nothing was offered to the all-Highest except that the frankincense was burnt when the bread was removed from the Table every Shabbos; and it is the memorial portion for the bread, for by means of it, it [= the bread] is remembered Above, similar to the fistful which is the memorial portion for the meal-offering.

he.t: המנחה הזאת, שכל דבר הבא מן התבואה, בכלל מנחה היא:

en.t: It shall belong —
this meal-offering, for any [offering] that comes from crops is [considered in the category of] meal-offering.

he.t: מוסב על הלחם, שהוא לשון זכר:

en.t: And they shall eat it,
referring to the bread, which is a masculine [noun].

he.t: מהיכן יצא, רבי לוי אומר מעולמו יצא, רבי ברכיה אומר מפרשה שלמעלה יצא, לגלג ואמר, ביום השבת יערכנו, דרך המלך לאכול פת חמה בכל יום שמא פת צוננת של תשעה ימים, בתמיה. ומתניתא אמרה (ת"כ פרשתא יד, א), מבית דינו של משה יצא מחוייב, בא ליטע אהלו בתוך מחנה דן, אמרו לו מה טיבך לכאן, אמר להם מבני דן אני, אמרו לו אִישׁ עַל דִּגְלוֹ בְאֹתֹת לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם (במדבר ב, ב) כתיב, נכנס לבית דינו של משה ויצא מחוייב עמד וגדף:

en.t: The son of an Israelite woman went out.

From where did he go out? R. Levi says: He went out of his [everlasting] world. R. Berechiah says: From the section above he set out [to ridicule]. He mocked [the showbread], saying: “’On each and every Shabbos he shall arrange them!’ It is the custom of a king to eat fresh bread every day, is it then [his way to eat] a cold loaf nine days old”? In astonishment. A teaching states: He went out guilty from Moshe’s court. He had come to pitch his tent in the midst of the tribe of Dan. They asked him: “What right have you to be here”? He said to them: “I am of the descendants of Dan.” They said to him: “Each man [shall camp] by his own flag, [that bears] the signs of their father’s house,” it is written He entered Moshe’s court and went out guilty. [whereupon] he stood up and blasphemed [= cursed].
And he was the son of an Egyptian man —
he was the Egyptian whom Moshe killed.
Among Bnei Yisroel —
[this] teaches that he was converted.
They argued in the encampment —
regarding matters [concerning] the encampment.

he.t: זה שכנגדו שמיחה בו מִטַּע אהלו:

en.t: And the Israelite man —
the one against him, who protested against his pitching his tent.

he.t: כתרגומו, וּפָרֵישׁ שנקב שם המיוחד וגדף (סנהדרין נו.), והוא שם המפורש ששמע מסיני:

en.t: Clearly pronounced,
as its Targum: “and he pronounced,” that he clearly pronounced the Proper Name, and blasphemed — it [the Name he used] is the Explicit Name he heard at Sinai.

he.t: שבחן של ישראל שפרסמה הכתוב לזו לומר, שהיא לבדה היתה זונה:

en.t: The name of his mother was Shelomis, daughter of Divri.
It is to the credit of Israel that this verse publicized this one, to say that she alone was a wayward woman.

he.t: דַּהֲוַת פטפטה שלם עלך, שלם עלך, שלם עליכון, מפטפטת בדברים, שואלת בשלום הכל:

en.t: Shlomis.
[She was called this] because she would chatter, “Be well”! “Be well” “Be well”! babbling [many] words, asking [about] everyone’s health.

he.t: דברנית היתה, מדברת עם כל אדם לפיכך קלקלה:

en.t: Daughter of Divri.
She was a chatterer, speaking with every person [who came her way], and therefore she became corrupted.

he.t: מגיד שהרשע גורם גנאי לו, גנאי לאביו, גנאי לשבטו, כיוצא בו אהליאב בן אחיסמך למטה דן (שמות לא, ו), שבח לו שבח לאביו שבח לשבטו:

en.t: Of the tribe of Dan.

[This] tells that an evil person causes disgrace to himself, disgrace to his father, disgrace to his tribe. Similarly, “Oholiov son of Achisomoch, of the tribe of Dan” — a credit to him, a credit to his father, a credit to his tribe.

he.t: לבדו, ולא הניחו מקושש עמו, ששניהם היו בפרק אחד, ויודעים היו שהמקושש במיתה, (סנהדרין עח:) שנאמר מְחַלְּלֶיהָ מוֹת יוּמָת (שמות שם יד), אבל לא פורש להם באיזו מיתה, לכך נאמר כִּי לֹא פֹרַשׁ מַה יֵּעָשֶׂה לוֹ (במדבר טו, לד), אבל במקלל הוא אומר, לפרוש להם, שלא היו יודעים אם חייב מיתה אם לאו:

en.t: They placed him [in the guardhouse] —

by himself, and they did not place the wood-gatherer with him, though the two of them were [in custody] during the same period of time. They knew that one who gathered wood [on Shabbos] was [condemned] to death, as it is said, “anyone who profanes it shall be put to death,” but the execution itself had not been explained to them. Therefore it is said, “For it had not been explained [to them] what should be done to him.” But regarding the blasphemer [the verse] says: “to explain to them” — for they did not know if he was liable to death or not.
Those who heard him. —
These are the witnesses.
All —
[this comes] to includes the judges.

he.t: אומרים לו דמך בראשך, ואין אנו נענשים במיתתך, שאתה גרמת לך:

en.t: Their hands.
They say to him: “Your blood is on your head, and we are not punished for your death, for you caused [it] to yourself.

he.t: במעמד כל העדה (ת"כ פרק יט, ג), מכאן, ששלוחו של אדם כמותו:

en.t: The entire congregation,
in the presence of the entire congregation. (From here) we learn that a man’s agent is like the man himself.
Shall bear [the burden] of his sin —
with koreis, when there is no warning.

he.t: אינו חייב עד שיפרש את השם, ולא המקלל בכינוי:

en.t: Whoever pronounces clearly —
he is not guilty until he pronounces the Name clearly, and not one who blasphemes by one of [God’s] titles.

he.t: לשון קללה, כמו מָה אֶקֹּב (במדבר כג, ח. סנהדרין נו):

en.t: And whoever pronounces.
“Pronounces” here is an expression of “cursing,” as [in the verse] “Why should I curse”?

he.t: לפי שנאמר מכה איש וגו' (שמות כא, יב), אין לי אלא שהרג את האיש, אשה וקטן מנין, תלמוד לומר כל נפש אדם:

en.t: Any man who kills.

Since it is said, “If one strikes a man and [the victim dies]” I [know that this applies] only when he killed a man, from where [do I know] [if he killed] a woman or minor? The verse [here] says: “any human being.”

he.t: פירשו רבותינו (ב"ק פד.) שאינו נתינת מום ממש, אלא תשלומי ממון שמין אותו כעבד, לכך כתוב בו לשון נתינה, דבר הנתון מיד ליד:

en.t: So shall it be done to him.

Our Rabbis explained that [this] does not [mean] placing an actual blemish [on him], but [rather] the payment of money. We appraise [his worth] as a slave [being sold in a slave-market]. Therefore [יִנָתֵן,] “giving” is written regarding it — something which is given from hand to hand.

he.t: למעלה דִּבֵּר בהורג בהמה, וכאן דבר בעושה בה חבורה:

en.t: Whoever smites an animal shall pay for it,
above (verse 18), [it] spoke of one who kills an animal, and here it speaks of one who causes a wound to it.

he.t: אפילו לא הרגו, אלא עשה בו חבורה, שלא נאמר כאן נפש, ובמכה אביו ואמו דבר הכתוב, ובא להקישו למכה בהמה, מה מכה בהמה מחיים, אף מכה אביו ואמו מחיים, פרט למכה לאחר מיתה, לפי שמצינו שהמקללו לאחר מיתה חייב, הוצרך לומר במכה שפטור, ומה בבהמה בחבלה, שאם אין חבלה אין תשלומין, אף מכה אביו ואמו אינו חייב עד שיעשה בהם חבורה:

en.t: Whoever smites a person shall be put to death,

even if he did not kill him, but [merely] caused a wound, for here [the word] “soul” does not appear. And of one who smites his father or his mother. [this] verse speaks, and [this verse is placed here] to compare [this case] to one who smites an animal: Just as one who smites an animal [when it is] alive [is liable], so [too] one who smites his father [when he is] alive [is liable] — excluding one who smites [his father or mother] after [their] death. Since we find that one who curses [one’s father and mother even] after death, is liable to the death[-penalty], it was necessary to state [the law] regarding one who smites [a parent’s body after death] that he is exempt [from the death penalty]. [The comparison goes the other way as well:] Just as [for wounding] an animal, [one must pay compensation], [for] if there is no wound there is no payment, so [too] one who strikes his father is not liable [to the death-penalty] until he causes a wound to him.

he.t: אלהי כולכם, כשם שאני מיחד שמי עליכם, כך אני מיחד שמי על הגרים:

en.t: For I am Adonoy, your God,
the God of all of you; just as I attach My Name to you, so I attach it to converts.

he.t: כל המצוה האמורה בסקילה במקום אחר דחייה, רגימה, ותלייה:

en.t: And Bnei Yisroel did —

[they carried out] the complete mitzvoh of stoning mentioned elsewhere [on the blasphemer]: casting [the condemned man down from a height], the heaping of stones [on him], and hanging [his body afterwards].
